prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1225; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received from the insured driver reporting a side impact at a signalized intersection, with the claimant seated in the front passenger position. The claimant is represented by counsel, and all further contact is being routed through the attorney's office.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the reported loss. No issues with the policy terms have been identified so far.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the scene and records the same sequence of events the insured described. The responding officer noted the impact point consistent with a vehicle entering the intersection from the side.

Entry 4: Reviewed scene photographs and statements from two independent witnesses, who both describe the collision as occurring just as the insured reported it. The other driver's statement matches on the sequence and location.

Entry 5: Inspected both vehicles. The damage pattern on the insured vehicle lines up with the reported side impact, and the repair estimate reflects damage consistent with that force. No prior damage to the vehicle has come to light in the records or photos reviewed.

Entry 6: Received the claimant's medical records through counsel. The reported knee injury fits the type and force of the crash, and the treating physician documented findings in line with that mechanism.

Entry 7: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Notes show steady improvement, and the frequency of visits tapered as the claimant recovered.

Entry 8: Prior records show a minor strain to the same knee area several years ago, which resolved completely with conservative care and has no bearing on the current complaint according to the treating physician's notes.

Entry 9: The claimant's account of the accident has remained the same across the recorded statement, the medical intake history, and conversations with counsel. Nothing in the file suggests the damage or injury predates the coverage period.

Entry 10: Reviewed the file with the claims supervisor, who agreed that the liability facts, vehicle damage, and medical course are all consistent with the reported loss. No further investigation steps are needed at this time.

Entry 11: Settlement discussions with counsel are proceeding on the basis of the documented medical treatment and property damage. File remains open pending receipt of the final billing and the demand package.
